Method of Attack: Ransomware-as-a-Service operation providing a ready-made toolkit (Toolbelt) that allows affiliates to download and execute various tools to steal passwords, spread laterally through networks, and deploy ransomware
Use of PowerShell scripts and executables to harvest credentials (Mimikatz, NirSoft Remote Desktop PassView, Hash Suite Tools Free), scan networks, and deploy ransomware
Affiliates compromise victims and deploy ransomware using the toolkit with remote desktop shared folder for executable delivery
Impacted Systems: Enterprise networks targeted by Dharma ransomware
Windows systems vulnerable to lateral movement and credential theft
Attack Vector: Compromise via Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) shares and execution of PowerShell scripts and executables from a mapped remote desktop shared folder
Affiliate access to victim networks using the toolkit to spread and deploy ransomware
Indicators of Compromise: Use of specific scripts and executables: toolbelt.ps1, purgememory.ps1, delete-avservices.ps1, processhacker-2.39-setup.exe, processhacker.exe, javsec.exe, ipscan2.exe, mstsc.exe, takeaway.exe, winhost.exe, ns2.exe, gamer.exe
File extension '.dharma' appended to encrypted files
